lines.hello: Welcome to Lit Town! Who is reading today?
lines.find-sound: Find the letter that makes this sound.
lines.find-in-text: Listen. Then find that word and tap it.
lines.new-sound: Here is a new sound. Listen.
lines.tap-and-say: Tap it and say it with me.
lines.new-sight: This is a tricky word. We just remember it.
lines.match-case: Find the small letter that matches the big letter.
lines.blend: Tap each sound. Then tap the arrow to read the word.
lines.read-it: Read it. Then tap the speaker to check.
lines.make-sense: Read it. Does it make sense? Tap yes or no.
lines.yes-or-no: Read it. Then tap yes or no.
lines.story-time: Story time! Tap any word if you need help.
lines.story-question: Read the question. Then tap yes or no.
lines.show-answer: Here it is. Let's keep going.
lines.lesson-pass: You did it! You earned flames!
lines.lesson-practice: Great practice! You earned a flame. Let's do this lesson again to open the next one.
lines.perfect: A perfect lesson! Here are extra flames!
lines.where-to: Where do you want to go?
lines.keep-reading: Keep reading, and this place will light up!
lines.town-lit: Your whole town is lit up! You did it!
lines.coming-soon: This place is still being built. Keep reading!
lines.need-more: You need a few more flames. Read a lesson to earn more!
lines.shop-hello: What would you like? Spend your flames!
lines.decorate: Tap your things to put them in your room or put them away.
lines.stuck: Stuck! This door won't open yet. Keep reading!
lines.door-open: The door is open! Let's go out on the deck!
lines.keep-fixing: Keep reading, and this will get fixed up!
lines.new-to-pick: There are new ones to pick! Tap the wrench to see them.
lines.pick-start: Listen to the sound. Which picture starts with it?
lines.match-pic: Read the word. Tap its picture.
lines.finish-it: Read it. Which word finishes it?
lines.clue-game: I'm thinking of an animal. Read the clues, then tap it!
lines.sort-it: Read each word. Put it in the right box.
lines.color-free: Color it any way you like!
lines.build-it: Build the word. Put the sounds in order.
lines.slow-down: Take your time. Read it first, then tap.
lines.stuck-teach: Let's look at this one together.
lines.pic-check: Read it. Does it match the picture?
lines.new-tricky: New tricky words for your shelf!
lines.tricky-shelf: Your tricky words! Tap one to hear it.
lines.tricky-shelf-empty: When you master a tricky word in a lesson, it goes up on this shelf!
lines.trace-watch: Watch the pen. Then follow it with your finger.
lines.trace-dotted: Trace the dots. Start at the green dot.
lines.trace-free: Now write it all by yourself.
lines.trace-word: Write the word. One letter in each box.
lines.trace-flip: So close! Your letter is facing the other way. Watch it turn around.
lines.trace-beside: Here is yours, next to mine!
lines.new-in-shop: You wrote it! Now it's in the shop.
lines.desk-hello: Your desk! Pick a board, then pick what to do.
lines.desk-no-name: Ask a grown-up to type your name first.
lines.desk-cleared: You practiced that letter so much, it's all done!
lines.placement-hello: Show me what you know! Listen, then tap. Some will be tricky, and that's okay.
lines.placement-done: Wow, you know so much! Let's read!
lines.step-back: Let's warm up with some easier ones!

lessons.title: Meet m, a and t
lessons.skill: m /m/, a /a/, t /t/; blend VC and CVC words
lessons.parentNote: Three sounds today, so she can read real words right away. Hold mmm, say a short a (as in apple), and a crisp t, not 'tuh'. Blend: mmm-aaa-t, mat.

lessons.title: Meet s and i
lessons.skill: s /s/, i /i/; tricky word: is
lessons.parentNote: 'is' is a tricky word: its s sounds like z. Questions start now: read it, then tap yes or no.

lessons.title: Meet p
lessons.skill: p /p/; tricky word: the
lessons.parentNote: p is a quiet puff of air: p, not 'puh'. Sorting: words that end in -at go in one box, -it in the other.

lessons.title: Meet n
lessons.skill: n /n/; CVC and blends with n

sentences.t: the ant is in the pan.
is the ant in the pan?

lessons.parentNote: Near-miss words today: pin, pan, pit. She has to look at every letter, not just the first.

lessons.title: Meet o
lessons.skill: o /o/; CVC and CCVC

sentences.t: the pot is on the mat.
is the top on the pot?

pages.t: a pot sits on the mat.
stop! a spot is on the pot!
tap it. mop it. tap, tap, mop!
the spot is not on the pot. it is on the mop!

question.t: is the spot on the mop?

lessons.parentNote: Short o as in octopus. First mini-story: tap any word to hear it.

lessons.title: Meet d
lessons.skill: d /d/; tricky word: I

sentences.t: dad and I sit on the sand.
is the pond on the pad?

pages.t: dad and I sit on a mat in the sand.
a pot, a pan and a tin.
an ant is on the mat!
the ant is in the pan! dad and I tip the pan.
and the ant is on the sand.

question.t: is the ant in the pond?

lessons.parentNote: d: tongue taps behind the top teeth. 'I' is always a big letter. Follow the directions: tap any colour, then tap the thing she read.

lessons.title: Meet c
lessons.skill: c says /k/; tricky word: to

sentences.t: can a cat sit on a cot?
can a cap sit on a cat?

pages.t: dad and I can camp.
a cat is in the camp!
the cat sat on the cot to nap.
I tap the cat. the cat is in a cap!
it is a camp cat.

question.t: did the cat sit on the cot?

lessons.parentNote: c usually says /k/ (cat, cap). Free colouring today: no right or wrong.

lessons.title: Meet g
lessons.skill: g /g/ (as in gift)

sentences.t: can a dog tag a cat?
can a pig spin a pan?

pages.t: a pig and a dog dig in the sand.
the dog got a cap!
tag! the pig got the cap.
the dog digs a pit. is the cap in it? it is!

question.t: did the pig tag the dog?

lessons.parentNote: g as in gift and dog (hard g). Listen for the first sound: g, d, or c?

lessons.title: Meet e
lessons.skill: e /e/ (as in egg)

sentences.t: ten eggs sit in a nest.
can a pet get in a tent?
I set the net on the tent.

clues: it can dig in the sand.
it can get in a pan.

pages.t: dad and I get the tent set.
I get in the tent. I get a pen and a pad.
a pet is in the tent!
it is the cat. it sits on the pad and naps.

question.t: did a dog get in the tent?

lessons.parentNote: Short e (egg) and short i (it) sound close: watch for pen/pin and pet/pit.

lessons.title: Meet u
lessons.skill: u /u/ (as in up); tricky word: was

sentences.t: the pup was in the mud!
can a pup dig up a nut?

pages.t: the pup was in the sun.
the pup dug in the mud. dig, dig, dig!
mud on the pup! mud on the mat!
I get a cup and a mop.
it is a mud pup, not a sun pup!

question.t: was the pup in the mud?

lessons.parentNote: Short u as in up. 'was' is tricky: it sounds like 'wuz'. The bakery lights up today!

lessons.title: Meet k and ck
lessons.skill: k and ck both say /k/

sentences.t: can a duck get stuck in the mud?
pack a snack and a cup.

pages.t: I pack a snack.
I sit on the dock. I get the snack.
a duck is on the dock!
the duck pecks at the snack. peck, peck, peck!
it is a snack duck!

question.t: did the duck get the snack?

lessons.parentNote: ck comes at the end of short words after a short vowel (duck, sock). Both k and ck say /k/.

lessons.title: Big letters
lessons.skill: Capital letters say the same sounds; names

teach.say: Big letters make the same sounds as small letters. Names and sentences start with a big letter.

sentences.t: Can a pig spin a pan?

pages.t: Tam can pat a cat.
Dot can dig in the sand.
Sid can spin a top.
And Pip? Pip can nap!

lessons.parentNote: Meet the four friends from the town. From now on sentences start with a capital and end with a period.

lessons.title: Meet r
lessons.skill: r /r/; r-blends (tr, dr, gr, cr); tricky word: of

sentences.t: A rat ran on the rug.
Can a truck run on a rug?
A cup of nuts is a snack.

pages.t: Tam got a red drum.
Tum, tum, tum! Tam can drum.
Pip ran in. "Is it a truck?"
Dot ran in. "Is it a rock?"
It is not a truck. It is Tam and a drum!

question.t: Did Tam get a red drum?

lessons.parentNote: r is a growl, not 'er'. 'of' is tricky: it sounds like 'uv'.

lessons.title: Meet h
lessons.skill: h /h/

sentences.t: The hen hid in a hut.
Dad had a hug and a hot cup.

pages.t: Sid had a tan hat.
Sid set the hat on a mat.
Tap, tap, tap! Up hops a hen!
Pip and Dot grin. The hen hums.
It was a hat trick!

lessons.parentNote: h is just a breath: h, not 'huh'. Sorting by first sound: h or r?

lessons.title: Meet b
lessons.skill: b /b/; tricky word: said

sentences.t: Can a bus get on a bed?

clues: It sits on a pad in the pond.

pages.t: Tam had a big bun.
It was the best bun!
Pip said, "Can I get a bit?"
Dot said, "Can I get a bit?"
Tam cut the bun in bits. Pip, Dot, and Tam had a bit.

lessons.parentNote: b vs d: b has its bump on the right (like a bat then a ball). Quote marks show someone talking.

lessons.title: Meet f
lessons.skill: f /f/; tricky word: you

sentences.t: The frog sat on a raft.
Can a bus fit in a cup?

pages.t: Pip and Dad set up a tent.
Fog! Pip can not spot the tent.
"Dad! Dad! Can you spot the tent?"
Dad gets a big fan. Puff, puff, puff!
Pip spots the tent! It is fun at camp.

question.t: Did Pip and Dad set up a tent?

lessons.parentNote: f: top teeth on the bottom lip, then blow. Free colouring again: anything goes.

lessons.title: Meet l
lessons.skill: l /l/; l-blends; tricky word: he

sentences.t: He can flip on the mat.

pages.t: Dot can flip on the mat.
Pip can flip on the mat.
Sid can flip. He runs fast and...
He slips! Bump!
Sid gets up. He can flip! Clap, clap, clap!

lessons.parentNote: l: tongue tip up behind the top teeth. Gymnastics story: 'flip' has an l-blend (fl).

lessons.title: Meet w
lessons.skill: w /w/; tricky word: are

sentences.t: Dot and Pip went to the pond.

pages.t: Dot and Pip are twins.
The twins swim in the pond.
"I will win!" said Dot. "I will win!" said Pip.
Swim, swim, swim! The twins are fast!
Dot and Pip get to the end. It is a twin win!

lessons.parentNote: w: round lips, like blowing out a candle. 'are' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet j
lessons.skill: j /j/; tricky word: she

pages.t: Dot can jump.
She jumps on the mat. Jump, jump, jump!
She jumps on a big rock.
She can not jump on a bus!
She jumps in the pond. Plop! It is fun!

question.t: Did Dot jump on a rock?

lessons.parentNote: j: like the start of jam. 'she' is tricky until we learn sh.

lessons.title: Meet x
lessons.skill: x says /ks/; tricky word: my

sentences.t: My fox is in a box!
Can an ox fit in a box?
Mix the jam in a cup.

pages.t: My gift is in a big box.
I tug and tug. It is stuck!
Mom helps fix it.
Pop! In the box is a red fox!
It is a soft fox. I hug it. It is the best gift!

question.t: Was a fox in the box?

lessons.parentNote: x makes two sounds together: k-s (box = b-o-ks). 'my' is tricky until we learn y. The park lights up today!

lessons.title: Meet v
lessons.skill: v /v/; tricky word: do

sentences.t: The vet can fix the pup.
Is the cat in a vest?
Dad has a big red van.

pages.t: Dot has a sick pup.
Mom and Dot get in the van.
The van stops at the vet.
The vet pats the pup. The pup will get well.
The pup is well! It licks Dot.

question.t: Did the vet help the pup?

lessons.parentNote: v: top teeth on the bottom lip, with a buzz (van). 'do' is tricky: the o says oo.

lessons.title: Meet y
lessons.skill: y says /y/; tricky word: they

sentences.t: Can a yak fit in a cup?
Yum! They had jam and buns.

pages.t: Sid has a big pot of yams.
The yams get hot in the pot.
Sid and Dot sit on the rug.
They get a yam. Yum, yum!
Dot yells, "Yes! It is the best yam!"

lessons.parentNote: y at the start of a word says /y/ (yes, yum). 'they' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet z and zz
lessons.skill: z and zz say /z/; tricky word: one

pages.t: One bug zigzags in the sun.
Buzz, buzz! It lands on the cap.
Sid gets up. The bug zips off!
It lands on a big red plant.
The bug sits on the plant. It is glad. Buzz!

question.t: Did the bug land on a plant?

lessons.parentNote: z buzzes like a bee. Two z's at the end (buzz) still make one sound. 'one' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet qu
lessons.skill: qu says /kw/; tricky word: have

pages.t: Dot has lost a quilt. It is red.
She hunts in the tent.
It is not in the box.
A duck quacks at the pond. Quack, quack!
The quilt is on the duck! The duck has a nap.

question.t: Was the quilt on the duck?

lessons.parentNote: q always comes with u: qu says /kw/ (quick). 'have' is tricky: the e makes no sound.

lessons.title: s can say /z/
lessons.skill: s at the end can say /z/ (dogs, has); tricky word: from

teach.say: At the end of a word, s can say z, like in dogs, has and his.

sentences.t: His dogs dig in the sand.
She has six pins from Mom.

pages.t: Sid has six dogs.
The dogs dig and dig in the sand.
His dogs run to the pond.
They swim and get wet.
Six wet dogs run from the pond to Sid. Sid gets wet!

lessons.parentNote: At the end of a word s often says /z/: dogs, has, his. Read it either way and listen for the real word. 'from' is tricky.

lessons.title: ff, ll and ss
lessons.skill: ff, ll, ss at the end of short words; tricky word: some

sentences.t: Some dolls sit on the bed.
Can a doll huff and puff?

pages.t: Some pups ran in the den.
They tug at a doll and a bell.
The milk spills on the rug. It is a big mess!
Mom huffs and puffs.
The pups help. They lick up the milk!

lessons.parentNote: At the end of a short word, f, l and s are often doubled: puff, bell, mess. The two letters make one sound. 'some' is tricky.

lessons.title: a or i?
lessons.skill: Short a and short i, near misses; tricky word: come

sentences.t: Come and sit on my lap.
Come in and sit. Dad has a snack.

pages.t: It is hot. Dot has a fan.
Sid comes in. He is hot.
"Come and sit," Dot said.
The fan spins and spins.
Sid and Dot sit and sip milk. It is not hot!

lessons.parentNote: A review of short a and short i. Near misses (pan/pin, hat/hit) teach her to look at every letter. 'come' is tricky.

lessons.title: o, u or e?
lessons.skill: Short o, u and e, near misses; tricky word: there

sentences.t: There is a nut on the log.
Is there a bed in the tub?
Is it hot in the sun?
There is a hut at the pond.

pages.t: There is a hut at the pond.
Sid and Dot get a net.
They sit on a log. They get a crab!
The crab nips the net. Snap!
They let the crab hop back in the pond.

lessons.parentNote: A review of short o, u and e: bed/bud, hot/hut. 'there' is tricky.

lessons.title: Long words
lessons.skill: Two-part words: sun-set, nap-kin; tricky word: what

sentences.t: Is a rabbit in the bucket?
Dad and I had a picnic at sunset.

pages.t: Mom and Dot have a picnic.
There is a big basket on the mat.
What is in it? Muffins and a napkin!
A rabbit hops up to the mat.
Dot hands it a bit of muffin. It is a fun picnic!

question.t: Did a rabbit come to the picnic?

lessons.parentNote: Long words are short words stuck together: sun + set, nap + kin. Cover half with a finger, read each part, then put them together. 'what' is tricky.

lessons.title: Quiz time!
lessons.skill: Review of lessons 21 to 29; tricky word: we

sentences.t: Can a van fit in a cup?

pages.t: We are at the big quiz. Dot and Sid sit up.
"What can buzz?" the man asks. Sid hits the bell. "A bug!"
"Yes!" said the man. Dot gets the next one.
"What has six legs?" Dot hits the bell. "An ant!"
We clap and yell. Dot and Sid win the quiz!

question.t: Did Dot and Sid win the quiz?

lessons.parentNote: A review of lessons 21 to 29. Read the story together twice: the second time, she reads it on her own. 'we' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet sh
lessons.skill: sh says /sh/; tricky word: me

sentences.t: Can a ship fit in a cup?
Hush! The cat naps on the shelf.

pages.t: Mom and Dot shop at the fish shop.
There is a big fish in a tank.
Dot wishes she had a fish.
Mom gets Dot a fish in a dish.
Dot is glad. Splash, splash! The fish swims.

lessons.parentNote: sh: two letters, one sound, like asking for quiet. 'me' is tricky: the e says its name.

lessons.title: Meet ch
lessons.skill: ch says /ch/; tricky word: be

sentences.t: Can we have lunch on the bench?
Can a chick be in an egg?
The chimp has chips at lunch.

pages.t: Sid has lunch on a bench.
He has chips and a big bun.
A chick hops up on the bench.
The chick pecks at a chip.
Sid hands the chick a chip. It munches it. Yum!

question.t: Did the chick get a chip?

lessons.parentNote: ch: like a sneeze, ch-ch-ch (chip, lunch). 'be' is tricky: the e says its name.

lessons.title: Meet tch
lessons.skill: tch says /ch/ after a short vowel; tricky word: her

sentences.t: She can catch it in her mitt.
Can a rock catch a fish?

items.t: I can _ it in my mitt.

pages.t: There is an egg in the hutch.
Tap, tap! The egg has a crack.
Dot sits still.
Pop! The egg hatches. It is a chick!
Dot sketches the chick in her pad.

lessons.parentNote: tch says /ch/ at the end of a word after a short vowel (catch, itch). The t makes no sound of its own. 'her' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet th
lessons.skill: th (quiet, as in thin); tricky word: who

sentences.t: Can a moth sit on a lamp?
Thump! Who is at the hut?

pages.t: Thump, thump! Who is on the path?
It is not a moth. A moth is thin.
It is not a cat. A cat can not thump.
It is a rabbit! It thumps on the path.
The rabbit hops off to the pond. Thump, thump!

lessons.parentNote: th: tongue between the teeth, just air (thin, bath). 'who' is tricky.

lessons.title: th can buzz
lessons.skill: th can buzz (this, that); tricky word: were

teach.say: th can also buzz, like in this, that and then.

sentences.t: We were at the pond, and then we went back.

pages.t: We are at the pond.
Then a duck swims up to us.
Then a frog hops on a log.
Then the sun sets.
That is the end of this fun trip.

lessons.parentNote: th has a second sound with a buzz in it (this, that, then). Feel your throat buzz. 'were' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet wh
lessons.skill: wh says /w/; tricky word: where

pages.t: Mom has a whisk. Where is it?
Is it in the pot? It is not.
Is it in the box? It is not.
Which pup has it? Sid's pup!
Mom gets the whisk. The pup gets a hug.

question.t: Did the pup have the whisk?

lessons.parentNote: wh says /w/ (when, whisk). Most question words start with wh. 'where' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet ng
lessons.skill: ng says /ng/; tricky word: your

pages.t: The king has a long song.
He sings it on the swing.
Ding, dong! The bell rings.
The king sings and sings. His song is long!
"Is your song at the end?" Dot asks. "Not yet!"

lessons.parentNote: ng is one sound made at the back of the mouth (sing, long). 'your' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet nk
lessons.skill: nk says /ngk/; tricky word: want

sentences.t: Think! What is in the trunk?

pages.t: Sid and Dot sit in the van. Honk, honk!
A skunk is on the path.
"I want to pet it!" Sid said.
"Think, Sid! It is a skunk!" said Dot.
Then the skunk runs off. Dot and Sid grin.

lessons.parentNote: nk sounds like ng with a k at the end (pink, think). 'want' is tricky: the a says o.

lessons.title: Endings: -ed
lessons.skill: -ed says /t/, /d/ or /id/; tricky word: could

teach.say: ed at the end means it already happened. It can say t, like jumped, d, like filled, or id, like landed.

sentences.t: The pup jumped up on the bed.
Sid kicked the can, and it landed in the pond.

pages.t: Dot and Sid fished at the pond.
The net filled up. It was a big fish!
The fish jumped and kicked.
Splash! It landed back in the pond.
Sid yelled, and then he grinned.

question.t: Did the fish land in the pond?

lessons.parentNote: -ed means it already happened. It says /t/ (jumped), /d/ (filled) or /id/ after t or d (landed). The e is often silent. 'could' is tricky.

lessons.title: Endings: -ing
lessons.skill: -ing endings; tricky word: would

teach.say: ing at the end means it is happening now: jumping, fishing, singing.

sentences.t: The pup is digging in the sand.
We are fishing at the pond.

items.t: The pup is _ in the sand.
The frog is _ on a log.

pages.t: Mom and Dot are fishing at the pond.
A frog is hopping on a log.
A duck is swimming. Quack!
Dot gets a tug. It is a fish!
"It can swim back," said Dot. Splash!

lessons.parentNote: -ing means it is happening now (jumping). Short words double their last letter first: swim, swimming. 'would' is tricky.

lessons.title: Blends with l
lessons.skill: l-blends: bl, cl, fl, gl, pl, sl; tricky word: should

teach.say: Two sounds can blend at the start of a word, like b and l in black. Say them fast: bl, black.

sentences.t: The flag is black and red.

pages.t: Dot has a black sled.
Sid and Dot drag the sled up the hill.
Then they sit on it. Zip! The sled slips and spins.
Flop! Dot and Sid land in a big drift.
"We should do that from the top!" said Sid.

lessons.parentNote: Blends are two sounds said fast together (bl, cl, fl, gl, pl, sl). If she stops between them, say both sounds, then say them faster. 'should' is tricky.

lessons.title: Blends with r
lessons.skill: r-blends: br, cr, dr, fr, gr, pr, tr; tricky word: two

teach.say: r can blend with the sound before it, like b and r in brick. Say them fast: br, brick.

sentences.t: Two crabs sit on a rock.
Fred has a red dress and a drum.

clues: It is wet and it can swim.
It can hop from a log to a rock.

pages.t: Fred and Dot get on a bus. It is a big trip.
At the pond, Fred spots a frog.
The frog grins at Fred. Fred grins back.
Then Dot spots two frogs on a big brick.
"Two frogs!" said Dot. "What a trip!"

lessons.parentNote: r-blends: br, cr, dr, fr, gr, pr, tr. Say the first sound and slide into the r. 'two' is tricky.

lessons.title: Blends with s
lessons.skill: s-blends: sc, sk, sm, sn, sp, st, sw; tricky word review: was

teach.say: s can blend with the next sound, like s and n in snap. Say them fast: sn, snap.

sentences.t: The skunk has a bad smell.

pages.t: Sam has a snack in a bag.
He sits on a swing to snack.
Then a skunk steps up.
Sam stops. The skunk sniffs the snack.
Sam lets the skunk snack. That was the end of the snack!

question.t: Did the skunk get the snack?

lessons.parentNote: s-blends: sc, sk, sm, sn, sp, st, sw. Hold the s, then slide to the next sound. 'was' comes back for practice.

lessons.title: Blends at the end
lessons.skill: end blends: -nd, -nt, -st, -mp, -lt, -ft, -sk, -lk; tricky word: put

teach.say: Two sounds can blend at the end of a word too, like n and d in pond. Say them both: nd, pond.

sentences.t: Put the lamp on the desk.
Can you put milk in a cup?
Put the gift on the desk.

pages.t: Mom hands Dot a gift.
Dot rips the top off the box.
In the box is a tent!
Dot and Mom set up the tent.
Dot gets in the tent with a lamp and her pup.

lessons.parentNote: End blends: -nd, -nt, -st, -mp, -lt, -ft, -sk, -lk. Make sure she says both last sounds (tent, not ten). 'put' is tricky.

lessons.title: Three-letter blends
lessons.skill: three-letter blends: scr, spr, str, spl, squ, shr, thr; tricky word: push

teach.say: Three sounds can blend at the start, like s, t and r in strap. Say them fast: str, strap.

sentences.t: The shrimp swim in the splash.
Push the swing, and I will hang on.

pages.t: It is spring. Dot and Sid run to the pond.
Sid sprints to the end of the dock.
Splash! Sid is in the pond!
Dot tugs Sid up on a strap.
Sid is wet, but he grins. What a thrill!

question.t: Did Sid splash in the pond?

lessons.parentNote: Three-letter blends: scr, spr, str, spl, squ, shr, thr. Go slowly, one sound at a time, then faster. 'push' is tricky.

lessons.title: The Lost Kitten
lessons.skill: Review of blends and short vowels; tricky word: pull

sentences.t: Is the kitten in the basket?

pages.t: Dot has a black kitten, Mittens.
Then Mittens is lost! Dot checks the basket. It is not in the basket.
Dot checks the shelf and the trunk. It is not there.
Then Dot spots a lump in the blanket. The lump twitches!
Dot pulls the blanket. It is Mittens! The kitten was in the blanket.

question.t: Was the kitten in the basket?

lessons.parentNote: A review of blends. The story is a little mystery: before the last page, ask her where she thinks the kitten is. 'pull' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet a_e
lessons.skill: a with silent e (cake, game); tricky word: give

sentences.t: Kate made a shape on the plate.

pages.t: Kate and Sid make a cake.
They bake it in a pan. Then they put it on a plate.
Kate can make a snake shape on the cake.
"We can name it The Snake Cake!" said Sid.
They give the Snake Cake to Mom. Mom has a big grin.

question.t: Is there a snake on the cake?

lessons.parentNote: Silent e makes the a say its name: cap becomes cape. The e at the end makes no sound. 'give' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet i_e
lessons.skill: i with silent e (kite, bike); tricky word: live

sentences.t: We live in a red hut.
Can a kite ride a bike?

pages.t: Mike has a white kite.
He can ride his bike up the hill with it.
The wind lifts the kite up and up.
It is the best kite on the hill!
Mike wins the prize. What a big smile!

lessons.parentNote: Silent e makes the i say its name: kit becomes kite. 'live' is tricky (it rhymes with give).

lessons.title: Meet o_e
lessons.skill: o with silent e (home, bone); tricky word: done

sentences.t: The dog is done with the bone.
Can a stone tell a joke?
Can a dog dig a hole?
I hope we get home in time.

pages.t: Rex the dog has a big bone.
He digs a hole and drops the bone in it.
Then Rex trots home.
Rex can nap. The bone is safe in the hole.
When Rex is done with his nap, he digs up the bone. Yum!

lessons.parentNote: Silent e makes the o say its name: hop becomes hope. 'done' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet u_e
lessons.skill: u with silent e (cute, tune); tricky word: gone

sentences.t: The mule has gone up the hill.
Is a cube a cute pet?

pages.t: June has a cute mule.
The mule can hum a tune with June.
Then the mule is gone!
June hums the mule tune. Hum, hum, hum!
The mule trots back to June. What a cute mule!

lessons.parentNote: Silent e makes the u say its name (cute, mule) or /oo/ (tune, flute, June). Try both and listen for the real word. 'gone' is tricky.

lessons.title: Meet e_e
lessons.skill: e with silent e (these, Pete), and silent e review; tricky word: love

sentences.t: Pete and Steve love to skate.

pages.t: Pete and Steve are twins.
These twins love to compete.
Pete can skate fast. Steve can ride a bike fast.
At the lake, the twins get to the end at the same time.
"We love to compete," said Steve. "Let us do it next June!"

lessons.parentNote: Silent e makes the e say its name: Pete, these, theme. Not many words use it, so this lesson also reviews a_e, i_e, o_e and u_e. 'love' is tricky.

lessons.title: Soft c
lessons.skill: c says /s/ before e and i (ice, face, cent); tricky word: once

teach.say: c can say s when e or i comes next, like in ice, face and mice.

sentences.t: Once, two mice ran a race.
Give me a slice of cake.

clues: It is wet and it can swim.
It can hop on a stone in the pond.

pages.t: Once, two mice made a space ship.
They put rice and a slice of cake in it.
Then they went up, up, up to space!
In space, the mice spin and race. What a nice place!
Then the mice came home. What a fun trip!

lessons.parentNote: c says /s/ when e, i or y comes after it (ice, face, cent). Before a, o and u it says /k/ (cat, cot, cup). 'once' is tricky.
